errors.text_span: The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is a linear scale from 0 to 65
errors.evidence: The y-axis actually ranges from 40 to 65, not 0 to 65.

errors.text_span: The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 52% at a co-occurrence number of $10^1$

errors.text_span: MEMIT method shows the second-highest accuracy, starting at about 45% and rising to approximately 55% at $10^3$

errors.text_span: The MEND method starts at about 45% and increases to around 56% at $10^3$
errors.evidence: MEND starts at approximately 45% but rises to approximately 56% slightly beyond $10^3$, not at $10^3$.

errors.evidence: FT starts at approximately 40%, not 41%, and rises to about 47%, not 48%, slightly beyond $10^3$.
